problem: The ISR only does ticks++ and never reloads TH0/TL0. In mode 1 (TMOD = 0x01, 16-bit, no auto-reload) the timer counts on from 0x0000 after overflow, so only the first interval is 1000 counts; every later interrupt comes after 65536 counts. The example therefore does not give regular timing, which is exactly what students will copy.
fix: Reload the count inside the ISR: void timer0_isr(void) interrupt 1 { TH0 = 0xFC; TL0 = 0x18; ticks++; } (or use mode 2 auto-reload, TMOD = 0x02, with 8-bit reload in TH0).

problem: Writing P1 = 0xFF to make P1.0 an input also turns every other pin of P1 into an input, wiping the outputs just set by P1 = 0x0F. A student reading only this line will corrupt the other pins.
fix: Write a 1 to only the pin being read: P1 = P1 | 0x01; then read P1.0. Say that each pin must have latch 1 before it is used as an input.

problem: "Mixing them causes address errors" is vague and misses the real restriction: sbit works only for SFRs whose byte address is bit-addressable (address ending in 0 or 8). TMOD (0x89) and SBUF (0x99) cannot have an sbit name.
fix: Say: an sbit can be declared only for a bit-addressable SFR (address ending in 0x0 or 0x8) or for bit-addressable RAM; sfr names a whole byte. To change one bit of TMOD, mask the byte with bitwise operators.

problem: "Small code and small data usually beat large models on an 8051 because code space and stack are limited." The data model does not consume program code space in that sense; the real cost of the large model is 16-bit pointers, extra pointer arithmetic and slow external-memory (MOVX) cycles.
fix: Say: small/compact models are faster because internal RAM is reached with direct and register addressing, while the large model needs 16-bit pointers and external-memory cycles; keeping data out of xdata also leaves internal RAM free for the stack.
